speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me the specific name of the antibiotic you were prescribed and for what condition?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Morbilliform Exanthem (Drug Eruption)

The clinical picture of a generalized, itchy rash appearing one week after starting amoxicillin for sinusitis, accompanied by fever and arthralgia, is highly suggestive of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction. Given the timing and distribution (starting in flexural areas and spreading), this is most consistent with a drug-induced maculopapular rash rather than an infectious etiology like viral exanthem or Kawasaki disease. Since the diagnosis is strongly supported by the temporal relationship and symptom profile, no further testing or questions are required to confirm this diagnosis.
